Subject: Harun and the training sign-up
Hi Uday,
You asked why I didn't issue Harun a warning for missing the forklift training sign-up again. I asked him about it on Friday. He told me he's been sleeping on a cousin's floor since his flat flooded in the monsoon, working our day shift and a night job, and often skipping lunch to save. He said the sign-up just slips out of his head. I believe him. When someone is running on so little, next month's course can't compete with tonight's bed. I've moved him to steady shifts, pointed him to the housing help desk, and told him lunch in the canteen is covered this month. I'll book the training for him in six weeks, once things settle. Can we keep this out of his file?
Pallavi

I'm Tarun. I run the tea stall outside the metro station in Hyderabad, and for most of last year, Anand was a regular.
He was a delivery rider, about twenty-four, always on his phone for orders. I found out slowly that he slept in a shared room with eight men and ate once a day, mostly my bun and chai. When the youth centre next door put up a poster for a free computer course, the other riders teased him: "Too lazy to fill a form?" He just shrugged and said, "Next month." Next month never came.
Then in spring a social worker from the centre helped him get a hostel bed and a meal card. Within weeks he looked different, less grey. One morning he borrowed my pen and filled that form, right here on my counter.
He wasn't lazy. He was just too tired and hungry to think past today.

I'm Jeevan. I used to get irritated with Sharmila, our neighbour in the chawl. She kept missing the free skills class I'd told her about. I thought, she doesn't want to improve.
Then her husband left and the roof over their room leaked all through the monsoon. I saw her sleeping sitting up, holding the baby away from the drip. She was working two cleaning jobs and eating whatever was left after the children.
One evening I asked about the class. She laughed, not happily. "Jeevan bhai, I don't know where I'll sleep next week. How can I think about a certificate?"
That was when I understood. It wasn't laziness. There was no room left in her head.
I got the housing committee to fix the roof. After that, she came to the class twice.

Sunday

Went to see Kunal today in his rented room near the station. He lost his job three months ago. He's been sleeping on a mat because the landlord took the bed back, and eating mostly bread. I tried to talk about his plans: courses, applications, the future. He just stared at me. 'I don't know about next month, Kamal. I don't even know about tomorrow's lunch.' I realised I'd been thinking he was lazy for not applying anywhere. He isn't lazy. His mind is full of rent and food. There's no room left for plans. So I stopped lecturing. I bought groceries, and I asked my cousin about the shelter with a proper bed near the station. Kunal called me tonight and said he'd slept properly for the first time in weeks. He asked me to help him write his CV tomorrow.

Kamal
